title: Tor intervals over a local ring and its strict henselization
statement:
Let $R$ be a local commutative ring with residue field $k$, let $k^{\mathrm s}$ be a separable closure of $k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and let $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselization of $R$ relative to $k^{\mathrm s}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Use unbounded derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For any $L\in D(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$ and integers $a\le b$, the following are equivalent:
(1) $H^i(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every degree-zero $R$-module $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$, where $L$ is restricted along $R\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$;
(2) $H^i(L\otimes_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}^{\mathbf L}P)=0$ for every degree-zero $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $P$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$.
The complex $L$ need not descend to $D(R)$; no Noetherian, finite-generation or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DK0, lemma-tor-amplitude-up-down-henselization, equivalence (1) with (3); apply its scheme formulation to Spec(R) at the closed point.

proof.text: Write $B=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. First assume (2). By [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model] over $B$, choose a flat $B$-module complex $E$ supported in $[a,b]$ and an isomorphism $E\cong L$ in $D(B)$. By [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness], every $E^i$ is also flat over $R$. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying groups and differentials unchanged, hence leaves $\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ unchanged and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. It therefore takes this derived isomorphism to an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Applying [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model] over $R$ to this same complex gives (1).

source.place: Tag 0DK0, lemma-tor-amplitude-up-down-henselization, (3) implies (1); flat-model version using Tags 0654 and 05VL.

proof.text: Now assume (1), and represent $L$ by a complex $K$ of $B$-modules. Since $R$ in degree zero is K-flat (tensoring with it is the identity), $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\cong K$. Taking $N=R$ in (1) gives $H^i(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$; this is also the $B$-module cohomology, since scalar restriction changes neither kernels nor images. Put $T^i=K^i$ for $i<b$, $T^b=\ker(d_K^b)$, and $T^i=0$ for $i>b$, with the induced differentials. The inclusion $T\to K$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees $i\le b$; in higher degrees both sides have zero cohomology. Thus $T\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $T$ is strictly zero above $b$.

source.place: Tag 0DK0, proof of (1) implies (3), obtaining the cohomological upper bound and truncating a representative.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] in the abelian category of $B$-modules to $T$, with upper bound $b$ and the class of all free $B$-modules. The class contains zero. Every $B$-module $M$ is a quotient of the free module $\bigoplus_{x\in M}B$, by sending its basis vector $e_x$ to $x$; this map is surjective because $x$ is the image of $e_x$. The cited lemma gives a quasi-isomorphism $P\to T$, all $P^i$ free, and $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Consequently $P$ represents $L$ in $D(B)$ and its restriction in $D(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0DK0, proof of (1) implies (3), choice of free resolution; Derived Categories Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, part (1).

proof.text: Each free $B$-module $B^{(I)}$ is flat: $B^{(I)}\otimes_B M\cong M^{(I)}$ by $e_i\otimes m\mapsto e_i m$, and a direct sum preserves exactness coordinate by coordinate, since every element has finite support. By [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness], every $P^i$ is therefore flat over $R$. The upper bound on $P$ lets [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] make $P$ K-flat over $R$, so $P\otimes_R N$ computes $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ for each $R$-module $N$. By (1), its cohomology in degree $a-1$ vanishes for every $N$. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] over $R$ to obtain flatness over $R$ of $Q=P^a/\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})$. This is a $B$-module, because the differential is $B$-linear, so [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness] makes $Q$ flat over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0DK0, proof of (1) implies (3), bottom cokernel; Tags 064K, 0653 and 05VL.

proof.text: Define $E^i=0$ for $i<a$, $E^a=Q$, and $E^i=P^i$ for $i>a$, with $d_E^a$ induced by $d_P^a$. This is well-defined since $d_P^a d_P^{a-1}=0$. The quotient map $P\to E$ induces the identity on $H^i$ for $i>a$ and the identification $\ker(d_P^a)/\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})=\ker(Q\to P^{a+1})$ at $i=a$. For $i<a$, $H^i(P)=0$ by step 2 and $H^i(E)=0$ by construction. Thus $P\to E$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $B$-complexes. The complex $E$ is supported in $[a,b]$, and its terms are flat over $B$ by step 4. The flat-model criterion [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model] over $B$ now gives (2), completing the equivalence.
